business_scope.primary_industry_name: Programmatic Real-Time Ad Exchange and SSP Platform

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - common law tradition at the provincial level in British Columbia, with a federal statutory overlay and constitutional supremacy (Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57 governs corporate formation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) - Canada-European Union investment protection
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA)
Canada-China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (in force October 1, 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and FINTRAC regulations; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, SC 1992, c 17; British Columbia Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, Part 3 as amended by the Business Corporations Amendment Act, 2022 (Bill 23), in force May 1, 2023 (BC Transparency Register); Land Owner Transparency Act, SBC 2019, c 23; judicial guidance on unlimited liability companies (BC/AB/NS ULC jurisprudence).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport for each UBO and each director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the individual's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for jurisdictions party to the 1961 Convention; if notarized in British Columbia, the BC Ministry of Attorney General Authentication Program issues the apostille)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency for any legal-person UBO holding 25% or more of shares or voting rights
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the UBO's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague-Convention jurisdictions, followed by certified English translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record / police clearance certificate for each director issued outside Canada
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police authority or accredited criminal-record bureau of the director's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or residency-consulate legalization with certified English translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized beneficial-ownership declaration (BC BCA Transparency Register particulars together with banking CDD declaration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: British Columbia notary or external legal counsel acting for the founding UBO(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization only; no apostille required for the internal corporate transparency register and bank CDD

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and significant counterparties against: (i) global PEP databases (Refinitiv World-Check, LexisNexis Bridger Insight); (ii) OFAC SDN List (prudent standard because USD-denominated Swift and ACH payment rails are targeted); (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) Canadian Consolidated Sanctions List administered by Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; (v) FINTRAC record-keeping and reporting obligations for the ongoing business. Standard customer due diligence is sufficient for this low-risk programmatic advertising platform; enhanced due diligence is automatically triggered by any PEP, adverse-media, or sanctions-list hit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: British Columbia Registries - 'Corporate Online' via the OneStop Business Registry (BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Citizens' Services)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names under BCA ss. 22-24 and BC Reg 45/2004 must be expressed in Latin (Roman) script; any trade name originating in a non-Latin alphabet must be transliterated into Roman characters. The legal designator is mandatory and must read 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', 'Societe a responsabilite illimitee', 'S.R.I.', or a prescribed combination. The proposed name must be distinctive and must not be confusingly similar to an existing name, trademark, or NUANS-listed mark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Trustee', 'Loan', 'Financial', 'Credit Union' (requires federal OSFI or BC Financial Services Authority consent)
'Securities', 'Investment', 'Mutual Fund', 'Exchange', 'Market' (securities exchange designation consent required under the BC Securities Act - critical review for an AdTech exchange brand)
'Royal', 'Her Majesty', 'Government', 'Canada', 'British Columbia', 'Parliament' (Crown and sovereign-connection consent required)
Terms contrary to public policy or obscene content (absolute prohibition under BCA s. 22(3)(d))
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a name request: (1) review the examiner's decision letter and NUANS report through the Corporate Online portal; (2) refile an amended name request, without additional documentation, while the original name search remains valid within the 56-day window; (3) where rejection is based on a conflicting existing name, obtain a written consent letter from the rightsholder and attach it to the resubmission; (4) file a written administrative reconsideration request with BC Registries (Registry of Companies, Service Delivery Team) within 30 days of the rejection; (5) if the dispute remains unresolved, apply to the BC Supreme Court for judicial review by petition under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c 241. Name request fees are non-refundable and each resubmission attracts a new statutory fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible. BCA s. 40(1) mandates a physical registered office and records office located in British Columbia at a street address; P.O. Boxes are expressly prohibited. A hosted 'virtual office' supplied by a professional registered-office provider is compliant if the provider physically displays the company name, accepts service of process at that BC street address, and stores statutory records in BC. Purely mail-forwarding virtual offices without a physical BC records address are non-compliant. For a programmatic AdTech platform with no BC employees, the standard structure is a law-firm or corporate-agent registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - below 5% annual probability for a low-risk, non-licensed entity. Likelihood rises to approximately 10-15% if the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) opens a GST/HST audit triggered by cross-border digital advertising revenue and non-resident payment flows, or if FINTRAC requests AML records. The BC Registry does not routinely conduct unannounced physical inspections absent a complaint, a default in annual reporting, or designated-guidance triggers.

Incorporation filing - ULC articles, notice of addresses, and notice of directors (online filing)

Statutory tariff - BC Reg 45/2004 (CAD 100 optional surcharge)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff under the Notaries Act, RSBC 1996, c 334 (CAD 150-200 per bundle market benchmark)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague apostille issuance - 3 notarized documents (BC Authentication Program)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: BC Ministry of Attorney General - Authentication Services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial license fee at prevailing market benchmark (USD 80 per screened individual)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional retainer at prevailing market benchmark (CAD 1,600-2,200 equivalent)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57 — ss. 10, 20-51, 196 (incorporation), ss. 424-433 (unlimited liability companies); Business Corporations Act Supreme Court Fees Regulation and Companies Regulation, B.C. Reg. 379/2002
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry, Registry Operations Division, Ministry of Finance (BC Registries, Victoria, BC)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form 1) filed electronically through BC Corporate Online (bcregistry.ca), accompanied by the prescribed Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement for a BC unlimited liability company (ULC). Shares may be issued without par value; no escrow account, capital deposit, or paid-up capital verification is mandated at formation. The ULC is an unlimited liability entity in respect of which the issued share capital provisions are contractually defined through the Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: THAT the subscriber hereby subscribes for and the Corporation allots and issues the authorized shares in accordance with the Notice of Incorporation and Articles; THAT the registered office of the Corporation be established at the address stated in the Notice of Incorporation and the records kept thereat; THAT the directors named in the Notice of Incorporation are confirmed in office; THAT the following officers be appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each with authority to execute banking and commercial agreements; THAT the Corporation adopts its Articles and initial by-laws; AND THAT the officers are authorized to effect all BC Corporate Registry and Canada Revenue Agency registrations necessary for lawful commencement of operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Pre-Approval and Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries Corporate Online (authorized name reservation service), Victoria, BC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name availability search through a BC Registries service provider; submit a name reservation request confirming the ULC designation is not required in the name but that the entity will operate as an unlimited liability company. Reserve the selected name for 56 days and record the reservation number for use in Form 1. If a simple name is desired without reservation, ensure the proposed name contains no statutorily prohibited or misleading terms.
required_dossiers: Name search report or NUANS equivalent
Contact and authorization details of the filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused because of confusion with an existing record, file an alternate name immediately using the same reservation queue, or apply for a decision review with BC Registries before the statutory refusal notice expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting Notice of Incorporation and Articles of the ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator's legal counsel; British Columbia Corporate Registry (destination filing body)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form 1 (Notice of Incorporation) together with the prescribed Articles to establish an unlimited liability company. Define share classes (typically Class A voting shares and Class B non-voting shares), record the registered office address in British Columbia, list first directors with consents, and define unlimited liability notice requirements for persons dealing with the company. Ensure all consents to act are dated prior to submission and retained in the incorporation records.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as first director(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Corporate Registry queries share class descriptions or director consents, correct the prescribed form and resubmit the amendment package; no re-filing fee is charged if corrected within the query response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission and Payment of Incorporation Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry (electronic filing window via BC Corporate Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to BC Corporate Online, enter the approved name, registered office address (must be a BC street address), first directors, and share structure, upload the executed Notice of Incorporation, pay the CAD $350.00 filing fee by credit card, and transmit the application for examination. Upon acceptance, the system posts the filing record and confirms the certificate issuance under s. 21 of the Business Corporations Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected or queried for data entry mismatches, the registry will issue a discrepancy notice; refile the corrected Form 1 electronically within 14 days to preserve the original requested effective date, or file a post-incorporation amendment if the incorporation has already been completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and Establishment of Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry (Registry Operations); incorporator and first directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retrieve the state-numbered Certificate of Incorporation in electronic form. Convene the first board of directors, adopt the pre-filed Articles and by-laws, approve the initial share subscription allotment, appoint officers, establish the registered office records, minute book, share certificate book, and register of directors. Issue physical share certificates to the initial beneficial owners of the ULC.
required_dossiers: Registers of directors and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory records are found defective during a registry inspection, cure by executing a directors' resolution ratifying the issuance, complete the register entries with retroactive effectiveness, and file any required Notification of Alteration (Form 10) to align the public record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Registration with the Canada Revenue Agency (Business Number and Tax Accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply through the CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) portal using the Certificate of Incorporation and the BC company number. Register the corporation for a nine-digit Business Number (BN), corporate income tax account, GST/HST account in the normal course, and payroll deductions account if employees will be hired. The BN, not the provincial registry number, is the federal identifier used for invoicing and tax filings.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation from BC Corporate Registry
Directors' personal information, Canadian residency status and date of birth
Registered office address in British Columbia
Incorporation date and fiscal year-end selection
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BRO application is rejected due to mismatched director identification or an unconfirmed BC incorporation number, retry the registration using the BC corporate record confirmation, or contact the CRA Business Window at 1-800-959-5525 to complete a manual registration and activate the BN without duplicating accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Bank Account Enablement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Vancouver Business Licence Office (or applicable BC municipality); Schedule B financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal business licence for a 'Software / Digital Technology Services' classification, specifying an office-based commercial premises. Simultaneously open the ULC's corporate bank account with Chrome/ACH/Wire payment rail enablement, presenting the Certificate of Incorporation, BN, corporate authorization resolution nominating signatories, and the directors' register to satisfy the bank's know-your-client verifications.
required_dossiers: List of directors and officers with identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality issues a zoning or use-classification query, amend the business licence application to the office/administrative classification and provide the software services description; if the bank defers the account opening, resubmit a corrected beneficial ownership schedule consistent with the ULC unlimited liability structure and the bank's AML/KYC requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — programmatic real-time ad exchange and SSP platform operations are unlicensed digital services in British Columbia. For incidental physical office premises, the applicable authorities are the municipal Business Licence office, Technical Safety BC (electrical and elevator safety), and WorkSafeBC (occupational health and safety).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial operating or manufacturing permit is required for an AdTech SSP platform. Optional but recommended: municipal business licence for office/administrative use; no industrial operating certificate is triggered under ISIC 7310.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable — BC Environmental Assessment Office, Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (review authority if physical infrastructure such as data centers were added)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration Not Required — pure software and cloud-based advertising exchange operations produce no physical discharge, no site disturbance, and are not listed as a reviewable project under the Environmental Assessment Act, SBC 2002, c. 43
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or air emissions are generated. Office operations remain subject to municipal sewer by-laws and solid waste recycling standards; energy consumption and cloud computing GHG emissions are voluntarily reported, with compliance applicable only if a physical data center or co-location facility is subsequently acquired.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety certification is mandatory for a pure cloud-based software operation beyond standard building code occupancy compliance. For any leased office, obtain: (1) municipal occupancy permit and fire marshal inspection clearance confirming means of egress and fire alarm compliance; (2) Technical Safety BC electrical permit for office fit-out and IT infrastructure installation; (3) WorkSafeBC employer registration and occupational health and safety clearance for workstations, ergonomics, and emergency procedures; (4) structural load inspection where server racks or heavy equipment are installed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Federal tax administration and principal GST/HST authority; CRA My Business Account portal at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html. British Columbia Ministry of Finance – Provincial Sales Tax (PST) and Employer Health Tax administration for provincial tax accounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A British Columbia unlimited liability corporation (ULC) is created under the Business Corporations Act (BC) through the BC Corporate Online registry. The federal Business Number (BN) and associated income tax account are generally established when CRA records are created after incorporation. If not auto-assigned, the corporation must apply by filing Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts' with CRA. Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada must similarly obtain a BN. For GST/HST, the ULC registers for a GST/HST program account through CRA Business Registration Online, Form RC1, or My Business Account. A valid Business Number plus GST/HST account number constitutes the statutory TIN for federal indirect tax purposes. BC PST account registration is made separately through the BC Tax Registration system (eTaxBC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Canadian tax resident corporation under Income Tax Act; no Canadian check-the-box. For U.S. federal tax purposes, a wholly-owned ULC may be eligible for check-the-box election as a disregarded entity / pass-through, but this does not alter Canadian entity-level taxation.)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Canadian domestic tax law. Available statutory elections relevant to a ULC include: voluntary GST/HST registration under the Excise Tax Act for markets below the mandatory threshold; section 216 Income Tax Act election for non-resident rental income; joint elections for closely-related corporations under GST/HST rules; and in the cross-border context, U.S. Form 8832 Entity Classification Election for U.S. check-the-box treatment (affecting only U.S. tax characterization). Hybrid mismatch rules under CFC and anti-deferral provisions may apply to the ULC's income in the owner's foreign jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Federal Goods and Services Tax); HST (Harmonized Sales Tax) applies in participating provinces only; British Columbia imposes separate PST (Provincial Sales Tax) at 7% on taxable goods and specified services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD $30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies made in Canada in any single calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; non-resident persons carrying on commercial activity in Canada exceeding this threshold must register for GST/HST. Voluntary registration is available below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing clearance, or digital stamping regime. CRA permits electronic invoicing and record-keeping, but does not require a government pre-clearance or digital tax stamp. GST/HST registrants with monthly or quarterly reporting periods must file returns electronically using GST/HST NETFILE, CRA's XML/API filing interface, or through a tax préparer. Records and third-party data supporting intra-community or export type supplies must be retained and made available on CRA audit request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A ULC may claim zero-rated GST/HST treatment on exports of goods and services. Tangible personal property is zero-rated if the supplier exports it as part of a supply of goods to a recipient outside Canada, with proof of export in the required form and timeframe. Services, including digital advertising and programmatic ad services, are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST and the service is for use wholly outside Canada; advertising services supplied to a non-resident for use in Canada are taxable. The supplier must retain documentary evidence demonstrating exportation and the non-resident destination/use. Input tax credits associated with zero-rated exports remain recoverable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) Export Declaration (B13A form or Electronic Export Reporting via CERS)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank wire transfer record proving payment in foreign currency from outside Canada
Copy of sales contract or service agreement identifying non-resident recipient and place of use
Proof of delivery outside Canada (including carrier tracking, terminal receipts, and customs destination stamps)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Excise Tax Act, CRA may reassess and claw back zero-rated treatment and input tax credits if export substantiation is deficient. False or dishonest statements in a GST/HST return attract a civil penalty equal to the greater of CAD $100 and 50% of the net tax or input tax credit claimed, plus arrears interest and compliance penalties. Knowingly evading payment or claiming fraudulent zero-rating may result in penalties under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act, including fines of up to CAD $25,000 or up to 200% of the amount sought to be evaded and imprisonment. CRA also applies a normal reassessment period of four years (longer in cases of misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud) and may assert the general anti-avoidance rule in respect of artificial export arrangements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) with prudential regulation and anti-money laundering oversight concurrently exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), and provincial securities/consumer protection authorities in British Columbia (BC Financial Services Authority) for non-prudential conduct.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible under both the current and capital accounts. Canada maintains a liberalized cross-border capital movement regime under the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements and the IMF Articles of Agreement Article VIII. There are no exchange controls, no approval thresholds, and no repatriation licensing requirements for current account transactions. Capital account inflows and outflows are generally unrestricted, subject only to statutory reporting, sanctions screening, and FATCA/CRS information exchange protocols. Dividends, management fees, royalties, interest, and proceeds from the disposition of shares in a BC Unlimited Liability Corporation (BC ULC) may be repatriated freely to foreign parent shareholders; however, remittances are subject to Canadian corporate income tax on the ULC's taxable Canadian income, Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (typically 25% absent treaty relief), and GST/HST obligations where applicable. A BC ULC that elects to be treated as a flow-through entity for Canadian tax purposes may nonetheless be subject to the branch tax under section 219 of the Income Tax Act upon remittances of branch profits to the offshore parent; advance rulings and professional tax advice are required to structure the optimum distribution and withholding framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in Canada. Exporters are not required to surrender foreign currency earnings to the Bank of Canada or any central authority. All export proceeds may be retained in freely convertible foreign currency accounts, such as USD or EUR settlement accounts maintained with Canadian Schedule I banks, or may be converted to Canadian dollars at any time through a licensed authorized foreign exchange dealer or bank. Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), FINTRAC reporting obligations apply to cross-border electronic funds transfers in excess of C$10,000, and to currency transaction reports of C$10,000 or more, irrespective of whether the proceeds are retained in foreign currency for service remittance through a programmatic advertising platform.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. The concept of an Electronic Money Institution (EMI) does not exist as a standalone regulated entity within the Canadian federal or British Columbia provincial banking framework. Digital banks, payment service providers, and fintech money-service businesses (MSBs) are subject to registration with FINTRAC and, if engaging in payment services, may need to be incorporated as bank or credit union subsidiaries under OSFI regulation. Offshore EMIs, such as UK FCA authorized EMIs or European e-money institutions, cannot hold Canadian dollar client funds nor provide local clearing account facilities in Canada without becoming a regulated Canadian MSB or obtaining a foreign bank branch licensing order from the Minister of Finance under the Bank Act. For a BC ULC programmatic AdTech entity, reliance on an offshore EMI is feasible only for non-Canadian denominated settlement flows where the offshore EMI has adequate Sanctions and FATCA/CRS compliance, but local CAD payroll, GST/HST remittances, and corporate payments should remain with a Schedule I Canadian bank. The ULC should therefore maintain a primary operational account with a tier-1 Canadian bank and use a regulated global FX/fintech platform strictly for optimized cross-currency conversions or as a secondary non-reserve settlement rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Federal and provincial regulations do not explicitly require directors or ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) to attend bank branches in person for all account types. The Client Identification and Verification Requirements under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act permit remote identification using a two-factor process: (i) a reliable digital identity verification service using government-issued ID; or (ii) an electronic verification of a credit file maintained by a Canadian credit bureau, matched by name, address, and date of birth. In practice, tier-1 Canadian banks will normally impose a video-conference interview or a notarized/certified true-copy attestation of identification documents for overseas directors and corporate UBOs of an unlimited liability corporation, because the ULC structure is uncommon and requires enhanced due diligence. A physical board meeting in British Columbia is also advisable to establish in-person corporate banking relationships, sign the banking resolution, and confirm the registered and records office address. Remote account opening is available with RBC, BMO, TD, Scotiabank, and CIBC for BC-incorporated companies via their business onboarding portals, but an international parent structure with non-resident directors will trigger additional documentary authentication and a designated relationship-manager interview conducted via secure video. To accelerate onboarding, the ULC should obtain a Canadian registered agent, a local BC physical business address, and a provincial Business Number (BN) from the Canada Revenue Agency before soliciting new accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership of the BC ULC is exercised through a non-resident parent entity or a trust/corporate chain involving high-risk jurisdictions, creating opacity for the bank's beneficial ownership register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a comprehensive corporate organizational chart from the offshore parent down to the BC ULC, showing every intermediate holding entity; obtain apostilled and certified certificates of incumbency for each layer; execute a subordinated beneficial ownership declaration for each individual UBO holding 10% or more of shares or control; supply passport copies and proof of residential address for each UBO; provide a written explanation of the commercial rationale for the ULC structure referencing the Canada-U.S. or relevant tax treaty N/A where applicable; and describe the AdTech platform's settlement flows, customer jurisdictions, and transaction velocity in plain language to satisfy 'source of wealth' requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business description of real-time programmatic ad exchange and SSP platform is considered by the bank's financial crimes unit as ambiguous, high-volume, third-party settlement facilitation with elevated exposure to cross-border payments from unvetted advertising counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the full contractual framework, including the platform's proprietary Ad Exchange Participant Agreement, SSP Publisher Terms, Advertiser/Media Buyer Terms, and Data Processing Addendum; provide independent registration or certification evidence that the platform is not required to be licensed as a Canadian securities dealer, money services business, or gaming operator; obtain a legal opinion from a British Columbia-qualified counsel confirming the business does not involve regulated financial services or gambling; provide audited financial statements, transaction-counterparty due diligence policies, and a Transaction Monitoring and Sanctions Screening policy document approved by the ULC's board; enumerate all traffic sources, anti-fraud certification (e.g., TAG Certified, Ads.txt/app-ads.txt), and third-party ad verification tools to demonstrate lawful ad delivery.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected high monthly wire volumes and expected large-value USD/CAD clearing through the account exceed the bank's ordinary threshold for non-resident owned small to mid-cap treasury accounts, triggering enhanced monitoring and possible account freeze.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed 12-month cash-flow projection segregating expected inbound advertising receipts (programmatic DSP deposits, SSP payout collections) from outbound inventory costs, technology hosting, payroll, and withholding taxes; map each payment type to an expected SWIFT purpose code and ensure no reportable transaction is structured to avoid the C$10,000 EFT or currency transaction reporting threshold; produce an enterprise-wide AML compliance manual and designate a Compliance Officer who will cooperate with the bank's annual compliance review; undertake to maintain at least 25% of monthly clearing volume as identifiable trade settlement to a permitted inventory of digital advertising impressions, programmatic inventory, or ad-server services; propose a cap-and-ramp structure where the bank raises transaction limits after 90 days of excellent performance and quarterly reviewed negative news screening reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or materially all shareholders are resident in a jurisdiction considered high-risk for money laundering or sanctions (e.g., offshore financial centres), causing the bank's client acceptance policy to classify the ULC as high-risk rather than standard risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a cross-border ownership and control explanatory memorandum detailing that the ULC's economic substance and decision-making remain centred in British Columbia through a local BC chief financial officer, a BC registered records office, daily bank operations executed by a BC based treasury back-office, and compliance personnel contracted in BC; provide certificates of good standing/beneficial ownership from the parent jurisdiction's corporate registry; deliver a sanctions list screening certificate for each director and UBO issued within 30 days; provide evidence of source of startup funds via bank statements and gift/equity agreements; accept conditions imposed by the bank including exclusion from intermediating payments for sanctioned or restricted jurisdictions, enhanced end-to-end transaction monitoring, and quarterly independent AML audit at the ULC's cost.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and working capital injections from a foreign parent into the BC ULC should be routed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 through the parent bank's correspondent relationship with a Canadian Schedule I bank. The Beneficiary Account should be the ULC's operational account at a tier-1 Canadian bank, with the Beneficiary line should clearly state the exact legal name and account number of the ULC. The purpose code should be populated with a cross-border payment narrative explicitly referring to 'Share Capital Contribution / Subscription for Common Shares of BC Unlimited Liability Company' in the remittance information field, and if the Canadian bank asks for FINTRAC EFT reporting information, thepayer and beneficiary must be identified by legal entity identifier or full physical address. For foreign direct investment (FDI) statistical reporting under the Balance of Payments framework, Statistics Canada relies on enterprise surveys rather than transactional exchange controls; the ULC should notify the CRA of its foreign ownership status through the-designated Canada Revenue Agency forms and provide supporting board resolutions, share subscription agreements, and proof of landed funds. The Canadian bank will also screen the remittance against Canadian sanctions lists and may require a completed source-of-funds questionnaire for inbound amounts exceeding C$250,000; the defence package should include the parent company's audited financials, the ULC's capital contribution minutes, and a written declaration that the funds are free of proceeds of crime. A separate legal entity escrow account may be opened concurrently for the exact deposit of subscription funds pending issuance of shares; the account should be styled as 'Capital Escrow – BC ULC – Share Subscription', with disbursement only against a share issuance resolution and statutory records update under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for trade obligations should be executed through SWIFT MT103 for high-value, one-time supplier payments, and through Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (L/C) for contracted media inventory or technology-hosted services when supplier credit terms and documentary conformity are required. For programmatic advertising inventory settled through DSP/SSP partners, the primary commercial clearing rail will be an automated ACH/Direct (ACH Business-to-Business) for low-value/polling-frequency CAD and USD disbursements, supplemented by SWIFT MT103 for cross-border partner payouts where the payee is not within the ACH network. All outbound wire instructions should attach the relevant CIS (Corporate Identification Structure) and include a purpose description such as 'Payments for Digital Advertising Media Brokerage Services', 'Infrastructure Software Subscription', 'Royalties for DSP SSP Technology Licensing', or 'Intercompany Management Fee' as supported by contracts. The bank should be supplied with a standing disbursement mandate authorizing same-day approvals up to an aggregate limit, with any disbursement above the limit requiring a second bank officer approval and the ULC's telex/SWIFT authentication by a two-person rule. L/Cs may be issued for substantive ad insertion orders with a clear presentation pack (commercial invoice, bill of lading/airway bill for physical assets, or certificate of digital delivery/performance for virtual ad impressions, publisher statement, and ULD statement). The governing law of all L/Cs should be UCP600, with availability by sight payment, and governed by the Canadian bank's international division to minimize documentary discrepancies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD deliverable outright forwards and FX swaps with a Canadian Schedule I bank under an ISDA Credit Support Annex (CSA), fully permissible for commercial hedging.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CAD/USD are available only where a physical delivery market is not operationally efficient; though the CAD is freely deliverable, NDFs are legally available from Canadian authorized FX dealers on a risk-adjusted basis.
Currency options (vanilla put/call) on CAD vs USD or on a parent's functional currency, fully permissible for hedging projected USD advertising revenue and CAD operational expenses.

Cross-currency swaps between CAD and USD, hedged with periodic exchange of notional and fixed/floating interest payments, permitted for maturity-matched capital structure swaps where the BC ULC has record financing.

Futures contracts on CAD/USD cleared through recognized Canadian derivatives clearing facilities, permissible regulatory-wise but operationally only if the ULC maintains a futures trading agreement and appropriate pre-trade risk limits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under the Business Corporations Act (annual confirmation/return updating current directors, members, and registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registries (Corporate Online portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after each anniversary of the company's incorporation or recognition date; anniversary-based, not calendar-year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of approximately USD 39 (CAD 53.50) in addition to the filing fee; after a default notice period (typically 30 days), the Registrar may administratively strike the company from the register and dissolve it, commonly after two consecutive missed annual reports; for a ULC, the unlimited liability of shareholders and director obligations continue to carry residual risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (or unanimous shareholder resolution waiving the AGM for the year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records - Minute Book, Register of Members, and resolutions; no government filing unless articles are amended
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once in each calendar year and no later than 15 months after the last preceding AGM; first AGM within 18 months of incorporation; waiver requires unanimous consent of all members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate registry dollar penalty, but persistent failure supports registrar strike-off for neglect or cessation, invalidates the audit-waiver procedure, and subjects directors to offence provisions under the Business Corporations Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal return also computes BC provincial corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; tax balance-due payable within 2 months after year-end (foreign-controlled ULC does not qualify for the CCPC 3-month balance-due extension)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Income Tax Act s. 162(1) late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month of delinquency (maximum 12 months), minimum CAD 100 when no tax is owing; CRA prescribed-rate interest accrues on unpaid amounts; repeat or egregious defaults may trigger prosecution or director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold is prescribed by the BC Business Corporations Act. A private (non-reporting) ULC must appoint an auditor at the annual general meeting unless the members unanimously resolve to waive the auditor for that financial period. A mandatory audit is triggered when the company is a reporting issuer under securities legislation, when the annual waiver resolution is not unanimous, or when lenders, investors, or the foreign parent's consolidation controls contractually require audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP as set out in the CPA Canada Handbook - IFRS is mandatory for reporting (publicly accountable) enterprises; a private ULC may elect either IFRS or Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) and must apply the selected framework consistently. For a ULC consolidated by a US parent, US GAAP reconciliation or a parallel GAAP pack is commonly required for the parent's 10-K or audit filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: British Columbia maintains no separate annual UBO declaration or beneficial-ownership filing for a private ULC. On every share transfer, the company must promptly update the Register of Transfers and Register of Members, recording transferors, transferees, date, consideration, and resulting ownership percentages, and must be able to produce beneficial-ownership records to CRA, FINTRAC, and regulators on demand. Federal T2 filing requires disclosure of the foreign-parent control structure; if the ULC acquires BC land, Land Owner Transparency Act reporting obligations apply.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 260 to 900 (CAD 350 to 1,200) per year - typical BC corporate-agent range covering statutory registered office, corporate-record custody, and annual report processing
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500 to 25,000 (CAD 10,000 to 35,000) - typical certified audit fee for an operational private BC ULC; not incurred if the members' unanimous audit waiver is in effect

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (federal 15% general rate + BC 12% general provincial rate; 11% combined for active business income eligible for the Small Business Deduction on first CAD 500,000)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction: federal 9% + BC 2% = 11% on first CAD 500,000 of eligible CCPC active business income; no ULC-specific Canadian tax holiday; federal Scientific Research & Experimental Development (SR&ED) ITC up to 35% non-refundable / 25% refundable; BC Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit (20% labour-related) if in qualified BC digital media
